body:
OBSERVED 2026-08-09. Surfaced by the CWNG KOBO session; the comment and the thread
were both read here before filing. NOT ACTIONED — see ownership at the bottom.

WHAT WE POSTED. new-usemame, 2026-05-19, janeczku/calibre-web#2610
(issuecomment-4483334439):

  "The 'where did they go' answer is they were always on the device. A
   community-maintained CWA-derived build (new-usemame/Calibre-Web-NextGen) can now
   import them from your KoboReader.sqlite and show them in the browser"
  + docker pull ...:v4.0.84 + the release link.

WHAT THE THREAD IS ACTUALLY ABOUT. Title: "Annotations on Kobo ebook disappear after
syncing with Kobo." Body: "the Kobo E-reader deletes all stored annotations from the
local database." Repro step 5: "Annotations are deleted and cannot be viewed again."

So the premise is wrong for this thread. The rows are NOT still on the device — their
absence from the device is the entire complaint. We told affected users to import from
a source the bug they are reporting had already emptied. Anyone who followed the advice
got an empty import and no explanation.

TO BE FAIR TO THE COMMENT: the import feature is real and it genuinely solves an
adjacent problem — annotations made on-device that the library never surfaced. It is
misapplied here, not fabricated. It reads like outreach pattern-matching on the word
"annotations" without the thread's mechanism being read.

A SECOND ERROR UNDERNEATH IT, from the KOBO investigation: the reporter attributes the
destructive reply to a self-hosted server. Stock calibre-web never redirected
reading_services_host — that is CWA/CWNG-era behaviour — so their annotations GET went
to KOBO'S OWN CLOUD, which has nothing for a sideloaded book. Correcting the
attribution moves the mechanism closer to us, not further away, because we are the
build that DOES redirect that host and proxy those verbs.

WHY IT IS RECORDED RATHER THAN FIXED. CLAUDE.md rule 4 permits upstream comments only
through the outreach flow: approved templates, after a release containing the fix,
skip-checks passed. A correction to our own earlier comment is not that, and the
outreach surface belongs to another session. Posting from here would be exactly the
unilateral upstream mutation the rule exists to prevent.

WHAT A CORRECTION WOULD HAVE TO SAY, if the operator wants one: that the import path
addresses annotations still present on the device, that it cannot recover rows Nickel
has already deleted, and — only if we are confident — what we now understand about
where the destructive empty reply originates. It should not be posted while that last
part is still uncertain; a second wrong answer on the same thread is worse than
silence.

STANDING LESSON FOR OUTREACH: the skip-checks gate WHEN we may post. Nothing gates
whether the reply fits the thread's mechanism. This one passed every mechanical check
and was still the wrong answer, because "annotations" matched and nobody read the
repro.

RELATED: F-30e824 (a shipped capability neither UI mentions), F-3b565b (CWNG KOBO's
data-integrity finding on the same endpoint). Credit: CWNG KOBO.
title: Our 2026-05-19 comment on janeczku#2610 answers a question the thread is not asking
